<section id="gy-location-hero">
  <div class="gy-location-hero-content">
    <span class="gy-location-kicker">California Food Forests &amp; Edible Landscapes</span>
    <h1>Growing Food in California</h1>
    <p>
      Explore food forests, edible landscapes, and home orchards across Arizona
      while discovering how growers work with desert heat, limited rainfall,
      winter cold, and carefully designed microclimates.
    </p>
  </div>
</section>

<main class="gy-location-main">
  <div class="gy-location-inner">

    <section class="gy-growing-intro">
      <div class="gy-growing-copy">
        <div class="gy-section-heading">
          <span class="gy-section-label">Growing in California</span>
          <h2>Different Regions, Different Ways to Grow</h2>
        </div>

        <p>
          Arizona ranges from extremely hot low-desert communities to much cooler
          high-elevation regions. That means there is no single Arizona growing climate.
          The food forests documented by The Green Yard are currently concentrated in
          the Phoenix metropolitan area, where long, intensely hot summers are paired
          with mild winters and occasional freezes.
        </p>

        <p>
          In the low desert, successful edible landscapes often depend on thoughtful
          placement, shade, mulch, irrigation, soil improvement, and microclimates.
          Winter sun can be valuable, while harsh summer afternoon sun may need to be
          reduced for subtropical and tropical plants.
        </p>

        <p>
          Rather than presenting one formula for growing in California, these tours
          are an opportunity to learn directly from the people doing the work:
          what they grow, why they grow it, what challenges they face, and how
          their landscapes change through experience.
        </p>
      </div>

      <aside class="gy-growing-note">
        <strong>About These California Tours</strong>
        <p>
          Most Green Yard Arizona tours currently feature the Phoenix metro and
          surrounding low desert. As the library expands, this page can also include
          food-growing systems from Arizona’s cooler and higher-elevation regions.
        </p>
      </aside>
    </section>

    <section class="gy-climate-section">
      <div class="gy-section-heading">
        <span class="gy-section-label">Climate Snapshot</span>
        <h2>California Growing Context</h2>
        <p>
          These conditions describe the Phoenix-area low desert where most of
          The Green Yard’s current Arizona tours are located.
        </p>
      </div>

      <div class="gy-climate-grid">
        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Climate</span>
          <strong>Highly Varied</strong>
          <p>Extremely hot, dry summers with abundant sunshine and mild winter conditions.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Growing Season</span>
          <strong>Varies by Region</strong>
          <p>Different crops peak in different seasons, with winter often providing excellent vegetable-growing weather.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Summer</span>
          <strong>Dry &amp; Variable</strong>
          <p>Temperatures above 110°F are possible and afternoon sun can be especially stressful for sensitive plants.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Winter</span>
          <strong>Regional Differences</strong>
          <p>Most winter days are mild, but occasional cold nights can damage tropical and subtropical plants.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Water</span>
          <strong>Dry Summers</strong>
          <p>Reliable irrigation, deep watering, mulch, and water-efficient design are central to productive landscapes.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-climate-card">
          <span>Common Theme</span>
          <strong>Adapt to Place</strong>
          <p>Shade, canopy, wind protection, thermal mass, and careful plant placement can significantly expand what is possible.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section>
      <div class="gy-section-heading">
        <span class="gy-section-label">The Growing Reality</span>
        <h2>What California Growers Are Working With</h2>
      </div>

      <div class="gy-opportunity-grid">
        <div class="gy-opportunity-card positive">
          <h3>Opportunities Growers Explore</h3>
          <ul>
            <li>A wide range of climates creates an equally wide range of crops</li>
            <li>Long growing seasons in many coastal and southern communities</li>
            <li>Strong traditions of home gardening, farming, and community growing</li>
            <li>Warm areas can support many subtropical fruits</li>
            <li>Different communities bring diverse crops and growing knowledge</li>
          </ul>
        </div>

        <div class="gy-opportunity-card challenge">
          <h3>Growing Challenges</h3>
          <ul>
            <li>Water availability and dry summer conditions in many regions</li>
            <li>Extreme heat in inland valleys and desert communities</li>
            <li>Cold, frost, or snow in other parts of the state</li>
            <li>Wildfire, wind, and other regional environmental pressures</li>
            <li>Conditions vary enough that growers must adapt to their specific location</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
